decisions.reason: After two years on the market, this software carries added sunk development and reputational commitment and remains highly central to the firm's publicly stated move toward integrated, data-driven airport operations.

Because this connectivity module builds directly on the established airport software stack and supports digital integration across apron operations, management is likely to continue backing it and view any shortfall as temporary.

Although billing software is less core than operational control products, the firm has already invested in extending its software-service scope and is therefore still more likely to persist than to reverse course quickly.
This monitoring software fits the firm's installed-equipment expertise, lifecycle services, and analytics direction, so continued commitment is likely after another year of market presence.

As a close-to-core resource management module linked to automated end-to-end airport operations, it benefits from both strategic importance and accumulated commitment, making withdrawal within a year unlikely.
